FACT_ID: sec12-F01 | anchor: A01
On roads, bicycle operators have the rights and responsibilities of car drivers. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> src:rdmv-nm-l:new-mexico-motor-vehicle-division-taxati:handbook:pdf-0028]

FACT_ID: sec12-F02 | anchor: A01
When overtaking a cyclist, keep safe clearance, aim for at least five feet, and pass only where safe and legal. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> src:rdmv-nm-l:new-mexico-motor-vehicle-division-taxati:handbook:pdf-0028]

FACT_ID: sec12-F03 | anchor: A01
Allow cyclists additional space and time to merge or use a turn lane. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> src:rdmv-nm-l:new-mexico-motor-vehicle-division-taxati:handbook:pdf-0028]

FACT_ID: sec12-F04 | anchor: A01
Treat a bicycle as a lawful slow vehicle, as you would a backhoe. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> src:rdmv-nm-l:new-mexico-motor-vehicle-division-taxati:handbook:pdf-0028]

FACT_ID: sec12-F05 | anchor: A01
Although cyclists usually stay right, they may lawfully use the lane’s center and occupy the entire lane when necessary. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> src:rdmv-nm-l:new-mexico-motor-vehicle-division-taxati:handbook:pdf-0028]

FACT_ID: sec12-F06 | anchor: A02
Typical reasons for a cyclist to occupy the full lane include preparing to turn left, avoiding a squeeze on a narrow street, or avoiding grates, debris and other hazards. [A01] [A02]
Source: [A02 -> src:rdmv-nm-l:new-mexico-motor-vehicle-division-taxati:handbook:pdf-0029]

FACT_ID: sec12-F07 | anchor: A02
With a cyclist on your right, avoid passing then making a sudden right turn; slow and merge behind the cyclist before turning. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> src:rdmv-nm-l:new-mexico-motor-vehicle-division-taxati:handbook:pdf-0029]

FACT_ID: sec12-F08 | anchor: A02
Expect unexpected movement or lane changes from some cyclists, particularly young children. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> src:rdmv-nm-l:new-mexico-motor-vehicle-division-taxati:handbook:pdf-0029]

FACT_ID: sec12-F09 | anchor: A02
Cyclists must follow traffic signals, signs and laws as car drivers do. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> src:rdmv-nm-l:new-mexico-motor-vehicle-division-taxati:handbook:pdf-0029]

FACT_ID: sec12-F10 | anchor: A02
The bicycle requirements described by the handbook include a bright front light and effective rear reflector at night. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> src:rdmv-nm-l:new-mexico-motor-vehicle-division-taxati:handbook:pdf-0029]

FACT_ID: sec12-F11 | anchor: A02
Cyclists must ride with traffic and make turns in the same manner as cars. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> src:rdmv-nm-l:new-mexico-motor-vehicle-division-taxati:handbook:pdf-0029]

FACT_ID: sec12-F12 | anchor: A02
The handbook requires cyclists to signal turns and stops by hand, with the gestures shown in its illustrations. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> src:rdmv-nm-l:new-mexico-motor-vehicle-division-taxati:handbook:pdf-0029]

FACT_ID: sec12-F13 | anchor: A02
Cyclists can improve conspicuity through bright clothing, suitable lighting and predictable movement. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> src:rdmv-nm-l:new-mexico-motor-vehicle-division-taxati:handbook:pdf-0029]

FACT_ID: sec12-F14 | anchor: A02
The source describes riding with the ordinary flow of traffic as the safest bicycle position in traffic. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> src:rdmv-nm-l:new-mexico-motor-vehicle-division-taxati:handbook:pdf-0029]

FACT_ID: sec12-F15 | anchor: A02
The manual advises well-fitting helmets for adults and states that minors must wear them. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> src:rdmv-nm-l:new-mexico-motor-vehicle-division-taxati:handbook:pdf-0029]

FACT_ID: sec12-F16 | anchor: A02
Sharrows are pavement symbols marking shared travel lanes. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> src:rdmv-nm-l:new-mexico-motor-vehicle-division-taxati:handbook:pdf-0029]

FACT_ID: sec12-F17 | anchor: A02
The handbook places sharrows where a road is too narrow for side-by-side sharing with slower vehicles. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> src:rdmv-nm-l:new-mexico-motor-vehicle-division-taxati:handbook:pdf-0029]

FACT_ID: sec12-F18 | anchor: A02
A sharrow encourages cyclists to use the full lane and requires motorists to yield when needed. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> src:rdmv-nm-l:new-mexico-motor-vehicle-division-taxati:handbook:pdf-0029]

FACT_ID: sec12-F19 | anchor: A02
At sharrows, motorists should reduce speed and yield to cyclists occupying the roadway. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> src:rdmv-nm-l:new-mexico-motor-vehicle-division-taxati:handbook:pdf-0029]

FACT_ID: sec12-F20 | anchor: A02
At sharrows, pass a cyclist only when roadway width permits the cyclist to move right. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> src:rdmv-nm-l:new-mexico-motor-vehicle-division-taxati:handbook:pdf-0029]

FACT_ID: sec12-F21 | anchor: A02
The sharrow guidance asks motorists to try for at least five feet of passing clearance. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> src:rdmv-nm-l:new-mexico-motor-vehicle-division-taxati:handbook:pdf-0029]

FACT_ID: sec12-F22 | anchor: A02
A cyclist may ride down the sharrow’s center. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> src:rdmv-nm-l:new-mexico-motor-vehicle-division-taxati:handbook:pdf-0029]

FACT_ID: sec12-F23 | anchor: A02
Cyclists should keep clear of the area where a parked car’s door may open. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> src:rdmv-nm-l:new-mexico-motor-vehicle-division-taxati:handbook:pdf-0029]

FACT_ID: sec12-F24 | anchor: A02
Cyclists should move right to allow a vehicle past when doing so is safe. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> src:rdmv-nm-l:new-mexico-motor-vehicle-division-taxati:handbook:pdf-0029]

Misconceptions: a bicycle may need the full lane; the source’s five-foot wording is a target, not an independently verified statutory minimum.
Mnemonics: leave room, wait behind before turning, and check the truck’s signals.
Glossary: a sharrow marks a shared lane; door zone is the space a parked vehicle’s opening door can occupy; NO ZONE means truck blind spots.
Dynamic facts: current bicycle law, roadway width, vehicle blind areas and changing traffic require checking.
